_comment: GLYPH GEOMETRY for the participant badges. ⛔ THIS FILE NO LONGER CARRIES COLOUR, and that is the point: the badge is now ONE AUTHORED MASTER (css/tokens.css, --vig-field / --vig-rim / --vig-halo) rather than a per-emoji derivation.

WHY THE DERIVATION WENT. Pulling the ground out of the emoji's own colours guarantees the worst case — a blue bicycle got a blue ground and 16% of its ink cleared 3:1. Measured across a neutral sweep from black to white, NO single flat ground works for all five: mid-tones drop the worst glyph to ~0% legible ink, white kills 🔑 and ☕, black kills 🚲.

WHAT REPLACED IT is what a real merit badge does — a constant field and a HALO on the emblem. The halo clears 16.5:1 against the field, so EVERY glyph has a guaranteed edge whatever its own colours are. That is why any emoji can be dropped in now.
WHAT IS STILL MEASURED, AND MUST BE. A flex box centres the LINE BOX, not the glyph, and every emoji fills its box by a different amount:
inkH  = inked height as a fraction of the box. 🚲 is 0.48 where 🌳/🔑 are 0.70 — the bicycle really is ~30% smaller at one font-size.
inkDy = how far the ink centre sits from the box centre (+down). 🚲 is +0.004 where the rest are about -0.09.

The generator turns these into a per-role scale (toward `inkTarget`) and a nudge. ⛔ RE-MEASURE WHEN YOU CHANGE AN EMOJI — the generator throws on a role with no ink block, and on an inkH near zero (which means the glyph did not render when captured, not that it is small).
TO RE-MEASURE: open the Ward on localhost and run the inkBox snippet from the commit that introduced this file.
